turns.en: As part of their fall season, which Maven just launched, there are over 100 new courses starting in the next few weeks. Many of the people I've had on this podcast are teaching courses like Jackie Bavaro on product strategy, Arielle Jackson on startup branding, Emily Kramer on B2B marketing, plus Annie Duke on decision making, Nir Eyal on behavioral design, and how to break into product management with Marily Nika. Check out all of my favorite courses and learn more at maven.com/lenny.
turns.zh: 作为 Maven 刚刚推出的秋季课程的一部分，未来几周将推出 100 多门新课程。我在这个播客中遇到的许多人都在教授课程，比如 Jackie Bavaro 教授产品策略、Arielle Jackson 教授初创品牌、Emily Kramer 教授 B2B 营销、Annie Duke 教授决策、Nir Eyal 教授行为设计，以及如何与 Marily Nika 一起进入产品管理领域。在 maven.com/lenny 上查看我最喜欢的所有课程并了解更多信息。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Now, again, I'm saying that as if it applies to all customers and products, and that's not actually the case. Sometimes it's more complicated than that, but in general, that is what we have found. So that's what we did for SparkToro customers based on the research that we did. The research that we do, we basically take all the responses, we identify the critical patterns, and that's how we identify the customer job. From those critical patterns, if we segment down just that customer job, we can look at responses and say, "Okay, here's what they're likely doing when they're out in the world experiencing this problem. This is how they described the pain of their current solution. And then here's what they say about how their search for a solution started. Here's what they told us about how they started to do that research or find a solution."
turns.zh: 现在，我再说一遍，好像它适用于所有客户和产品，但实际情况并非如此。有时情况比这更复杂，但总的来说，这就是我们发现的。这就是我们根据我们所做的研究为 SparkToro 客户所做的事情。我们所做的研究，基本上会收集所有的回复，确定关键模式，这就是我们确定客户工作的方式。从这些关键模式中，如果我们只细分客户的工作，我们可以查看回复并说：“好吧，这就是他们在外面遇到这个问题时可能会做的事情。这就是他们如何描述当前解决方案的痛苦。然后这是他们如何开始寻找解决方案的。这是他们告诉我们他们如何开始进行这项研究或找到解决方案的。”

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And then there's questions that are asked in the research like, "What was the moment that convinced you that our product was going to solve this problem for you?" And the answers to that question are going to tell you what your first value should look like, which of that first product activation experience, whatever language you like to use, what should that look like for them? What parts of the product do you need to push right up to the front of that experience so they can get to it really, really quickly after they sign up?
turns.zh: 研究中会提出一些问题，例如“是什么时刻让您相信我们的产品将为您解决这个问题？”这个问题的答案将告诉您您的第一个价值应该是什么样子，第一个产品激活体验是什么，无论您喜欢使用什么语言，对他们来说应该是什么样子？您需要将产品的哪些部分直接推到该体验的最前面，以便他们在注册后能够非常非常快地使用它？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And then value realization obviously would be close to, if not, the desired outcome of that customer job where you're solving that customer job. And then you've got all kinds of... Generally, what happens when I'm going through this process with teams is, all kinds of ideas start to come up about what more they could be doing, even post solving that customer job, especially the product team gets really exciting because they've got all kinds of ideas about where the product can go. So that really helps tie everybody together too.
turns.zh: 然后，价值实现显然会接近（如果不是）您正在解决客户工作的客户工作的预期结果。然后你就会得到各种各样的……一般来说，当我和团队一起经历这个过程时，会发生各种各样的想法，关于他们还可以做什么，甚至在解决客户工作后，特别是产品团队变得非常令人兴奋，因为他们对产品的发展有各种各样的想法。所以这也确实有助于将每个人联系在一起。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: A critical part of that process obviously is identifying we have to measure success along the way. There should be a KPI for each of those stages in that customer journey. And for the most part, they won't be a big surprise on the struggle side of things. People out in the world experience the problem, how are we going to know we're doing a good job reaching them? We bring in new unique website visitors. In general, that would be the measure of success for the problem milestone. And then next piece of the puzzle is like, okay, once they discover that we exist, even if they are visiting, reading product reviews and visiting competitor sites or whatever, we'll know we've done a good job of convincing them that we can help solve their problem and deterring the people that we don't want.
turns.zh: 该过程的一个关键部分显然是确定我们必须一路衡量成功。客户旅程中的每个阶段都应该有一个 KPI。在大多数情况下，在事情的斗争方面，它们不会让人大吃一惊。世界各地的人们都遇到过这个问题，我们如何知道我们在帮助他们方面做得很好呢？我们带来了新的独特网站访问者。一般来说，这将是衡量问题里程碑是否成功的标准。然后下一个难题是，好吧，一旦他们发现我们的存在，即使他们正在访问、阅读产品评论和访问竞争对手的网站或其他什么，我们就会知道我们已经很好地说服了他们，我们可以帮助解决他们的问题并阻止我们不想要的人。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: We know we've done a good job when the conversion rate on whatever our primary CTA is on our website, whether or not it's start a trial or request a demo, something like that. Generally, the struggle phase is very straightforward in terms of measurement. That's like marketers' bread and butter, that's where they live and breathe all day long. Where things start to change though generally when we're working with companies is helping them figure out how should they be measuring first value or product activation and how should they be measuring actual product engagement. Generally, what we do there is, we can associate basically what they told us brings them the most amount of value with the product attribute or parts of the product that deliver that value. We try to tie the KPI obviously to some sort of meaningful product usage of that key part of the product or product attribute.
turns.zh: 我们知道，当我们网站上的主要 CTA 的转化率很高时，无论是开始试用还是请求演示等，我们都做得很好。一般来说，斗争阶段的衡量方法非常简单。这就像营销人员的面包和黄油，是他们整天生活和呼吸的地方。一般来说，当我们与公司合作时，事情开始发生变化，帮助他们弄清楚应该如何衡量第一价值或产品激活，以及他们应该如何衡量实际的产品参与度。一般来说，我们所做的就是，我们基本上可以将他们告诉我们给他们带来最大价值的东西与产品属性或提供该价值的产品部分联系起来。我们试图将 KPI 明显地与产品或产品属性的关键部分的某种有意义的产品使用联系起来。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Can you share some examples of that? Because that's a really important piece.
turns.zh: 您能分享一些例子吗？因为那是非常重要的一块。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah. I'll use SparkToro as an example just because it's the one that we started with. So for SparkToro, I don't remember the exact customer job statement necessarily, but for them, what they said were, the parts of the product that gave them a ton of value was two specific features: lists. So being able to organize their findings in a way that made it not only easy for them to organize within their own files but also share because a lot of them were with clients or stakeholders that they want to be able to share with. So lists were a specific feature that honestly, it was in there, but they weren't front loading the product experience with that. I'm not going to say it was hidden, but it wasn't front and center enough. So that was one feature that we could associate with being able to organize the data, being able to continue to build on it and make it usable over time and also share.
turns.zh: 是的。我将使用 SparkToro 作为示例，因为它是我们一开始使用的。因此，对于 SparkToro 来说，我不一定记得确切的客户工作声明，但对他们来说，他们所说的是，产品中给他们带来大量价值的部分是两个特定功能：列表。因此，能够以某种方式组织他们的发现，不仅使他们可以轻松地在自己的文件中进行组织，而且还可以进行共享，因为其中很多都是与他们希望能够共享的客户或利益相关者共享的。所以列表是一个特定的功能，老实说，它就在那里，但他们并没有预先加载产品体验。我不会说它是隐藏的，但它不够前面和中心。因此，这是我们可以将其与能够组织数据、能够继续构建数据并使其随着时间的推移可用并共享相关联的一项功能。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And then there was another feature as well, which was an exporting feature. Again, it's not that it was hidden, but it wasn't front and center enough. So we tied KPIs to them making use of those features, coupled with obviously the core feature, which is searchability. It was like pairing the search functionality with the list functionality, and then pairing the search functionality with the list functionality, with the export functionality. It's a bit abstract to me just saying the words. It's easier with a visual. But the story is basically, help them use the search functionality first. Right after that, make sure that they're using lists. And if they don't use lists, let's help them get back to using it so that they get to that important critical value moment. And then the same applies for the exporting features that we were talking about.
turns.zh: 然后还有另一个功能，那就是导出功能。再说一次，并不是它被隐藏了，而是它不够前面和中心。因此，我们利用这些功能将 KPI 与它们联系起来，再加上明显的核心功能，即可搜索性。这就像将搜索功能与列表功能配对，然后将搜索功能与列表功能以及导出功能配对。光是说这些话对我来说有点抽象。通过视觉更容易。但故事基本上是，首先帮助他们使用搜索功能。之后，确保他们使用列表。如果他们不使用列表，让我们帮助他们重新使用列表，以便他们到达那个重要的关键价值时刻。这同样适用于我们正在讨论的导出功能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. And to be clear, you basically said a metric for each of these moments.
turns.zh: 知道了。需要明确的是，您基本上为每个时刻都说了一个指标。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah, milestones.
turns.zh: 是的，里程碑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Milestones. Yeah.
turns.zh: 里程碑。是的。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Or just whatever. I mean you have to. I mean it always surprises me when a team is like, "Oh yeah. Yeah, you're right, we don't do that." I'm like, "What? What do you mean?" So at a given milestone, unless they've reached that value moment, you can't keep them on the train to something else. If they haven't even discovered that really, to them, most valued part of their product, you would need to focus on getting them to that value. Otherwise, you can't just keep firing off emails and hoping they're going to jump back into the product as if they're going to care. So a lot of what we'd do is actually proactive customer experiences, whether or not in app or email or whatever tool, to help them get to that moment within the product.
turns.zh: 或者只是随便什么。我的意思是你必须这样做。我的意思是，当一个团队说“哦是的。是的，你是对的，我们不这样做”时，我总是感到惊讶。我说：“什么？你什么意思？”因此，在某个特定的里程碑上，除非他们已经达到了那个价值时刻，否则你不能让他们继续前往其他地方。如果他们甚至还没有发现，对他们来说，他们的产品中最有价值的部分，你就需要集中精力让他们实现这个价值。否则，你不能只是不断地发送电子邮件并希望他们会跳回产品，就好像他们会关心一样。因此，我们所做的很多事情实际上是主动的客户体验，无论是在应用程序、电子邮件还是其他工具中，以帮助他们在产品中达到那个时刻。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And if they don't get to that moment, which is measurable, again, that's why it's a KPI, then we can be reactive in helping them get back in. So identifying, "Okay," not that you would say this like, "it fell off the train," but just helping them nurture them back into, the product didn't really discover that feature if they missed it the first time around. So it's proactive and pushing them forward, but then also catching them if they fall. And the only way to catch them if they fall is if you're measuring something meaningful along the way.
turns.zh: 如果他们没有到达那一刻，这是可衡量的，这就是为什么它是关键绩效指标，那么我们可以做出反应，帮助他们重新回来。所以识别，“好吧”，不是你会说“它从火车上掉下来”，而是只是帮助他们培育他们重新回到，如果他们第一次错过了这个功能，产品并没有真正发现这个功能。所以它是积极主动的，推动他们前进，但如果他们跌倒了，也会接住他们。如果他们跌倒了，抓住他们的唯一方法就是你一路上测量一些有意义的东西。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: We have that storyboard that we were talking about. We also have a map where it's the experience to get them to a certain value moment, but then that win back experience to get them back in should they fall out for any reason. I mean, people get hungry and get distracted, and there's a ton of reasons why. I mean there's a lot of stats on the percentage. I think it's like 70% of people log into an app, log into a product once and never come back. It's wild. So the fact that so many companies don't have some sort of win back or re-engagement always blows my mind.
turns.zh: 我们有我们正在谈论的故事板。我们还有一张地图，其中的经验可以让他们到达某个价值时刻，但如果他们因任何原因退出，则可以赢回经验让他们重新回来。我的意思是，人们会感到饥饿并分心，原因有很多。我的意思是有很多关于百分比的统计数据。我认为这就像 70% 的人登录应用程序、登录产品一次后就再也没有回来过。它很狂野。因此，这么多公司没有以某种方式赢回或重新参与的事实总是让我感到震惊。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So just to recap and then we'll keep going with the process. Step one, understand what your customers are going through, figure out the most important customer and their biggest problem, then map out the journey that they go through, the struggle they go through before they discover your product, the steps they go through to evaluate, decide to use your product. And then once they use your product, then continuing to use your product and using it more and more. And then once you figured out these steps... And is a rough number like 10, 12 steps? What's a good number just to put-
turns.zh: 回顾一下，然后我们将继续这个过程。第一步，了解你的客户正在经历什么，找出最重要的客户和他们最大的问题，然后规划出他们经历的旅程，他们在发现你的产品之前经历的挣扎，他们评估、决定使用你的产品所经历的步骤。一旦他们使用了你的产品，就会继续使用你的产品，并且越来越多地使用它。然后，一旦你弄清楚了这些步骤……粗略的数字是 10 步、12 步吗？一个好的数字是多少——

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Oh no, I would hope it's more like six.
turns.zh: 哦不，我希望它更像是六个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Six, okay.
turns.zh: 六个，好吧。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: I'm always trying to bring it down lowest, only as long as it absolutely needs to be. I mean that goes for all pages, landing pages.
turns.zh: 我总是试图把它降到最低，只有在绝对需要的时候。我的意思是这适用于所有页面，登陆页面。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, all right.
turns.zh: 好吧，好吧。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Same thing for customer journey mask.
turns.zh: 客户旅程面具也是如此。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Airbnb had 12, I think. So you're involved in-
turns.zh: 好的。我想 Airbnb 有 12 个。所以你参与了——

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I liked that. Okay. And then you've come up with a metric to tell you if that step is performing well.
turns.zh: 我喜欢那个。好的。然后您提出了一个指标来告诉您该步骤是否执行良好。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: If they'd gotten there, did they get to that value?
turns.zh: 如果他们到达了那里，他们达到了那个价值吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If they've gotten there. Cool. One last question before we move on to the next step. Can you give two maybe examples of an actual movement, say in SparkToro's case, and then the metric that they use to measure, if they've gotten to that point?
turns.zh: 如果他们已经到了那里。凉爽的。在我们继续下一步之前还有最后一个问题。您能否给出两个可能的实际运动示例（例如 SparkToro 的案例），以及他们用来衡量的指标（如果他们已经达到了这一点）？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yes. So the measure for success at that tip somebody over into evaluation is performing their first search. So when you're on their website, you perform a search, it's not signing up for a trial or signing up for free, although it does tip you into signing up for free when you perform your first search. So signing up for getting your first search and seeing your first search results is that first measure. And then following that for first value, it is using search again. I mean this is very product specific like I said, but generally, a first search is a kind of an experiment where you're sort of trying the tool on for the first time. Generally, searches start to get better when you do your second and third. So we try to encourage at least five plus.
turns.zh: 是的。因此，衡量某人是否成功的标准是进行第一次搜索。因此，当您在他们的网站上执行搜索时，这并不是注册试用或免费注册，尽管它确实会在您执行第一次搜索时提示您免费注册。因此，注册获得您的第一次搜索并查看您的第一个搜索结果是第一个措施。然后，在第一个值之后，它再次使用搜索。我的意思是，正如我所说，这是非常特定于产品的，但一般来说，第一次搜索是一种实验，您是第一次尝试该工具。一般来说，当您进行第二次和第三次搜索时，搜索就会开始变得更好。所以我们尽量鼓励至少五个以上。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: So that first value KPI, I think it was five plus searches, plus at least one list. So it's the combination of those two things that have to happen before somebody's going to really see what this thing does. It's not that they won't get value if they don't use lists, but because we know that SparkToro's ideal customers really get a ton of value out of lists, people can hang out in that stage all day long if they want to. We're not going to worry about them. We're going to worry about the people that really want the actual functionality of the real fully featured tool. So that was the first value, that's how we would know that they got to product activation.
turns.zh: 因此，第一个值 KPI，我认为是五个加搜索，再加上至少一个列表。因此，在人们真正了解这个东西的作用之前，必须先将这两件事结合起来。这并不是说如果他们不使用列表就不会获得价值，而是因为我们知道 SparkToro 的理想客户确实可以从列表中获得大量价值，所以如果人们愿意，他们可以整天在这个阶段闲逛。我们不会担心他们。我们会担心那些真正想要真正功能齐全的工具的实际功能的人。这就是第一个值，这就是我们如何知道他们已激活产品的方式。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And then the next one, as I mentioned before, is a combination of actually three things. So it is conducting a minimum amount of searches within a span of time, creating at least a certain number of lists, I can't remember exactly what it is, and then discovering exporting at least once. And then that is, they've reached a meaningful enough threshold of product engagement. And then value growth was that they do all of that on a regular enough basis so that we know they're not a flight risk basically. So that we know that they're getting continued value from the product. And if they ever fall out of that ongoing engagement measured success, then we can trigger either one-on-one outreach, an email, whatever. I mean obviously it can't be an app because if they're not logging into the app, then you can't reach them. But to help them back in and to say, "Hey, what's up? Can we help? Is there anything that we can do?" And basically be proactive in getting them back in. And then value growth, I believe I think it was expansion or upgrade in their case. I can't remember exactly.
turns.zh: 然后，正如我之前提到的，下一个实际上是三件事的组合。因此，它在一段时间内进行最少量的搜索，创建至少一定数量的列表，我记不清它到底是什么，然后发现至少导出一次。也就是说，他们已经达到了足够有意义的产品参与门槛。然后价值增长是他们足够定期地做所有这些事情，这样我们就知道他们基本上不存在逃跑风险。这样我们就知道他们正在从产品中获得持续的价值。如果他们脱离了持续参与衡量的成功，那么我们可以触发一对一的外展，一封电子邮件，等等。我的意思是显然它不可能是一个应用程序，因为如果他们没有登录该应用程序，那么你就无法联系到他们。但要帮助他们回来并说：“嘿，怎么了？我们能帮忙吗？有什么我们可以做的吗？”基本上要积极主动地让他们回来。然后是价值增长，我相信我认为对他们来说这是扩张或升级。我记不太清了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. So you end up with these say, six KPIs.
turns.zh: 凉爽的。因此，您最终会得到六个 KPI。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I imagine this becomes goals you track, and then you probably pick one of these to focus on say, per year, per quarter. Awesome.
turns.zh: 我想这会成为你跟踪的目标，然后你可能会选择其中一个目标来关注，比如每年、每季度。惊人的。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah, hopefully not per year.
turns.zh: 是的，希望不是每年。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, per week.
turns.zh: 好吧，每周一次。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Hopefully short, because I mean I will say that with some of the KPIs, it's very straightforward with new unique website visitors or the website conversion rate. I mean depending on who owns the website, that's not something that should take you a year. You should never be focused on only your website's conversion rate for a year hopefully. But these other KPIs and these other milestones, I mean I have no disillusions about if it impacts the product, obviously there's a lot of implications there. So yes, generally, once you tip over into that sort of in-app and more product experience, timelines vary widely, to say the least.
turns.zh: 希望很简短，因为我的意思是我会说，对于一些 KPI，新的独特网站访问者或网站转化率非常简单。我的意思是，这取决于网站的所有者，这不会花费您一年的时间。希望您永远不应该只关注网站一年的转化率。但这些其他关键绩效指标和其他里程碑，我的意思是，我对它是否会影响产品没有失望，显然那里有很多影响。所以，是的，一般来说，一旦你进入那种应用内和更多的产品体验，至少可以说，时间表差别很大。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, cool. Let's move on to the next step.
turns.zh: 好吧，酷。让我们继续下一步。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Okay. So after that point, we had a rich voice of customer document that came out of that research. We had a messaging guide for them to use not only in their marketing materials but also through the entire product experience, and also identifying the parts of the product that were so meaningful. Actually, their VP of marketing, the new VP of marketing, Amanda Natividad, actually rolled out checklist. They built a checklist, a product onboarding checklist and also product onboarding emails. And their trial-to-paid doubled. We were like, "Okay, cool, let us know if you need any help or whatever." And they're like, "Oh, we're good. We got this." Checked in two months later and their trial-to-paid had doubled.
turns.zh: 好的。因此，在那之后，我们从该研究中获得了丰富的客户声音文档。我们为他们提供了一个消息传递指南，不仅可以在营销材料中使用，还可以在整个产品体验中使用，并确定产品中非常有意义的部分。事实上，他们的营销副总裁、新任营销副总裁阿曼达·纳蒂维达 (Amanda Natividad) 实际上推出了清单。他们建立了一个清单、一个产品入门清单以及产品入门电子邮件。他们的试用付费倍增。我们说：“好吧，好吧，如果您需要任何帮助或其他什么，请告诉我们。”他们会说，“哦，我们很好。我们做到了。”两个月后检查，他们的试用付费增加了一倍。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel like you skipped the important staff of, "Hey, we got KPIs." And then you're like, "Oh, we gave them all this information." So I'd love to spend a little more time on there. You came up with messaging for them, positioning stuff. what happens there?
turns.zh: 我觉得你跳过了重要的部分，“嘿，我们有 KPI。”然后你会说，“哦，我们给了他们所有这些信息。”所以我很愿意在那里多花一点时间。你为他们想出了消息传递、定位的东西。那里会发生什么？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Well, this is the thing. They have a team in place. They've got very highly skilled, a huge team but highly skilled marketer there at the helm. I mean not the list of which is Rand Fishkin, their CEO. So basically, what we did was we gave them, it's like a framework. So it's like, "Here are the bones of this. So got a messaging and positioning guide for you." Generally, I mean when we do them, they're five to seven pages long. They hit on the value prop. They hit on the major competitive advantages. They hit on the major value themes that you want to focus on. Those value themes can be broken down by the emotional benefits and the functional benefits tied to the product attributes that drive that value. So that document, and there's more that goes into it, but that messaging guide basically can be used as the baseline for all kinds of marketing collateral and material, but also email onboarding.
turns.zh: 嗯，就是这样。他们有一个团队。他们拥有一支技术非常高超、团队庞大但技术高超的营销人员来掌舵。我的意思不是他们的首席执行官兰德·菲什金（Rand Fishkin）的名单。所以基本上，我们所做的就是给他们，它就像一个框架。就像是，“这是这件事的核心。因此，我们为您提供了消息传递和定位指南。”一般来说，我的意思是当我们做它们时，它们有五到七页长。他们抓住了价值支柱。他们抓住了主要的竞争优势。他们击中了您想要关注的主要价值主题。这些价值主题可以通过与驱动该价值的产品属性相关的情感效益和功能效益来细分。因此，该文档以及更多内容，但该消息传递指南基本上可以用作各种营销材料和材料的基准，也可以用作电子邮件入门的基准。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: So when they're writing their email sequences for whatever it is they're trying to solve for, whatever milestone they're solving for, they can use that as their baseline like, "This is what we're going for. This is the goal here." And that messaging guide rules up to the job to be done. So the job to be done is sort of like the top line. And then we've got that messaging that serves that job to be done. And then we've got the sort of operationalized customer experience with those milestones and KPIs. And then you sort of zoom in on like, where is the experience most broken right now? We already knew that for SparkToro. We knew that we wanted to influence that first early product experience. So that's where we zoomed in and decided on what programs they should roll out. And email onboarding was a natural, as was the checklist.
turns.zh: 因此，当他们为他们想要解决的任何问题编写电子邮件序列时，无论他们要解决什么里程碑，他们都可以使用它作为基线，例如“这就是我们想要的。这就是这里的目标。”该消息传递指南决定了要完成的工作。所以要完成的工作有点像顶线。然后我们就得到了为完成这项工作服务的消息。然后我们就通过这些里程碑和 KPI 获得了可操作的客户体验。然后你会放大看，现在体验最糟糕的地方在哪里？对于 SparkToro，我们已经知道这一点。我们知道我们想要影响第一个早期产品体验。因此，这就是我们放大并决定他们应该推出哪些计划的地方。电子邮件入职是很自然的事情，清单也是如此。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For folks that want to work on messaging, say kind of just like, "Hey, here's a bunch of messaging advice," any tips for how to message well, how to think about messaging once you have a sense of your journey, maybe some goals, any just pro tips here you could share?
turns.zh: 对于那些想要从事消息传递工作的人来说，可以说“嘿，这里有一些消息传递建议”，任何有关如何良好地传递消息的技巧，一旦您了解了自己的旅程如何考虑消息传递，也许是一些目标，或者您可以在这里分享的任何专业提示？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Oh, boy. I mean that research and the voice of customer, I mean I'm always going to go back to that. You can guess and you can do use your best judgment. You can use internal stakeholders and the internal team knowledge. And I'm not saying that that is not valuable and that you shouldn't use that at all. You can, but it should never come before learning from and listening to your best ideal customers and using the language that they use. You want to reflect them back to them. That is what is going to show them that you understand the problem that they have and that your product has exactly what it is that they need.
turns.zh: 哦，男孩。我的意思是研究和客户的声音，我的意思是我总是会回到这一点。您可以猜测，并且可以运用您的最佳判断。您可以利用内部利益相关者和内部团队知识。我并不是说它没有价值并且你根本不应该使用它。你可以，但在向最理想的客户学习、倾听他们的意见并使用他们使用的语言之前，永远不应该这样做。你想将它们反映给他们。这将向他们表明您了解他们所面临的问题，并且您的产品正是他们所需要的。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: The hierarchy of messaging is really important as well. So I mean, there's the classic, sometimes it's hard to see the label from inside the jar, so it's really helpful to get out and be like, "Okay, how do customers see us?" Generally, you can identify the hierarchy of what is important to them, what is the thing that they say is most valuable about their product? What was that aha moment or what was that first value moment? Or what is the thing that makes you stand out over everybody else? And it can literally be a numbers game. If you take a hundred or so survey responses, you can break that down like, "Here's the thing they said they cared about most. Here's the thing they said they cared about second most and third most," not to be so paint by numbers about it, but there's art in the science. But in general, you want to reflect back what they said they care about, not what you think is the coolest thing about your product. That's obviously not the best way to go.
turns.zh: 消息传递的层次结构也非常重要。所以我的意思是，这是经典的，有时很难从罐子里面看到标签，所以走出去并说“好吧，顾客如何看待我们？”真的很有帮助。一般来说，您可以确定对他们来说重要的层次结构，他们认为他们的产品最有价值的是什么？那个顿悟时刻是什么，或者第一个价值时刻是什么？或者是什么让你比其他人脱颖而出？它实际上可以是一个数字游戏。如果你收集了一百个左右的调查回复，你可以将其分解为，“这是他们说他们最关心的事情。这是他们说他们最关心的事情。”不要用数字来描述它，但科学中有艺术。但总的来说，你想要反映他们所说的他们关心的事情，而不是你认为你的产品最酷的事情。这显然不是最好的方法。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: That's something that we all inherently know, but it becomes really hard when there's a lot going on and things are changing and the product is evolving and there's a lot of teens and people are coming and going. It's easy to lose sight of that, especially when you're just trying to get shit out the door. So that messaging guide is mentally like, "Okay, here we are. This is my baseline, these are my guardrails for everything that we produce." It's also really handy to hand off to copywriters when you bring in... I mean not just copywriters, lots of people, but particularly when you're producing copy, providing that messaging guide is solar platter for them.
turns.zh: 这是我们本质上都知道的事情，但当发生了很多事情、事情在变化、产品在不断发展、有很多青少年和人们来来往往时，这就变得非常困难。人们很容易忽视这一点，尤其是当你只是想把屎扔出去的时候。因此，该消息传递指南在心理上就像是，“好吧，我们在这里。这是我的基线，这些是我们生产的所有产品的护栏。”当您引入时，将其交给文案撰写人也非常方便……我的意思不仅仅是文案撰写人，还有很多人，但特别是当您制作文案时，提供消息传递指南对他们来说是太阳能拼盘。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is this available anywhere, the template that you end up sharing with a customer? Just like, here's a guide, the layout, messaging, recommendations.
turns.zh: 您最终与客户共享的模板是否可以在任何地方使用？就像，这里有一个指南、布局、消息、建议。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Oh, we have so many.
turns.zh: 哦，我们有这么多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe a little-
turns.zh: 也许有一点——

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: We have so many templates and stuff. Yeah, I'll include a couple links.
turns.zh: 我们有很多模板和东西。是的，我会添加几个链接。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Great. I'll put it in the show notes.
turns.zh: 伟大的。我会把它写在演出笔记里。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: We got lots of stuff like that. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我们有很多这样的东西。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, great. A few final questions around jobs to be done.
turns.zh: 好的，太好了。关于要完成的工作的最后几个问题。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So you said that they doubled their conversion from free to paid.
turns.zh: 所以你说他们从免费到付费的转化率翻了一番。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. What was their job to be done in the end? And then I just have a few questions about the jobs to be-
turns.zh: 惊人的。他们最终要做什么？然后我有几个关于工作的问题-

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: I think it was when they're struggling to identify opportunities that aren't as obvious. So generally, when you're doing marketing research, you'll end up signing the same things over and over again. And if you are a service provider or if you're in-house for that matter and you're tasked with always coming up with novel and new and more and more and more, you tap that pretty quickly. So what customers were coming to them for was like, "Give me more. I need to impress here. I need more to work with. I need to identify opportunities that I wouldn't otherwise be aware of." Actually that was exactly what it was. I helped me identify opportunities as I wouldn't otherwise be aware of. So the customer job statement is, "When I am in a certain situation, help me," which is filled in by what those things that they're looking, for those motivations, "so I can," which is the desired outcome.
turns.zh: 我认为这是当他们努力寻找不那么明显的机会时。因此，一般来说，当您进行营销研究时，您最终会一遍又一遍地签署相同的内容。如果您是服务提供商，或者如果您是内部人员，并且您的任务是始终提出新颖的、越来越多的内容，那么您很快就会点击它。因此，客户来找他们的目的是，“给我更多。我需要在这里留下深刻的印象。我需要更多的合作。我需要发现我原本不会意识到的机会。”事实上，事情正是如此。我帮助我发现了我原本不会意识到的机会。因此，客户的工作声明是，“当我处于某种情况时，帮助我”，其中填写了他们正在寻找的东西，出于这些动机，“所以我可以”，这是期望的结果。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: The help me was about, I believe it was in a way that is organized and that is shareable and usable over time that I can build on and really rely on over time. And the desired outcome was about, I mean this isn't going to be surprising, but it was about getting stakeholder by hand and getting people on board with, and sharing and looking good, looking like a pro, and doing their job more effectively and driving better results for either their own team or for their clients.
turns.zh: 我相信它是一种有组织的、可共享的、可使用的方式，随着时间的推移，我可以继续构建并真正依赖它。期望的结果是，我的意思是这不会令人惊讶，而是要亲自让利益相关者参与进来，让人们参与进来，分享并看起来不错，看起来像专业人士，更有效地完成工作，为自己的团队或客户带来更好的结果。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. We got there. We gloss a little bit over jobs to be done. I imagine many people listening have no idea what this is. So maybe as our final question, can you just explain what this framework is and how folks can learn to use it, or any resources you recommend that comes to mind?
turns.zh: 惊人的。我们到了那里。我们稍微掩盖了一些需要完成的工作。我想很多听的人都不知道这是什么。因此，也许作为我们的最后一个问题，您能否解释一下这个框架是什么以及人们如何学习使用它，或者您推荐的任何资源？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah. I mean a heavy influence for us definitely is Bob Moesta, who's one of the original architects of jobs to be done. There are lots of materials online for jobs. I am not the foremost authority in jobs at all. I think jtbd.info is a good website. There's a bunch. Also, Bob Moesta wrote a book called Demand-Side Sales that goes into it. There's also a lot of books written about jobs to be done. When Coffee and Kale is one that a lot of people love. I digress. Point being that what matters is identifying what it is that customers are trying to accomplish. So demographic data doesn't matter. The classic example is, if you look at... Oh, King Charles, now the example has changed. If you look at Ozzy Osbourne, and it was Prince Charles the original, but now it's King Charles, if you look at those two men, they're the exact same age and live in the same area. They both have a dog. They both love cars.
turns.zh: 是的。我的意思是，对我们产生重大影响的肯定是鲍勃·莫埃斯塔（Bob Moesta），他是待完成工作的原始架构师之一。网上有很多工作材料。我根本不是工作方面的最高权威。我认为 jtbd.info 是一个很好的网站。有一堆。此外，鲍勃·莫埃斯塔 (Bob Moesta) 写了一本名为《需求方销售》的书，其中对此进行了探讨。还有很多关于要完成的工作的书籍。当咖啡和羽衣甘蓝是很多人喜欢的一种时。我离题了。重点是，重要的是确定客户想要实现的目标是什么。所以人口统计数据并不重要。经典的例子是，如果你看……哦，查尔斯国王，现在例子已经改变了。如果你看看奥兹·奥斯本，原来是查尔斯王子，但现在是查尔斯国王，如果你看看这两个人，他们的年龄完全相同，住在同一地区。他们都有一只狗。他们都喜欢汽车。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: From a demographic standpoint, they are identical, but they obviously lead very different lives. What motivates them is very different. So that is where typically personas sort of fall down. So what jobs to be done, to us, is help you figure out what is that desired outcome, what does that better life that customers are seeking out. You were just the vehicle to get them there. That's all it is. I mean there's so many tired analogies so I don't even want to use them but-
turns.zh: 从人口统计学的角度来看，他们是相同的，但他们的生活显然截然不同。他们的动机非常不同。这就是角色通常会失败的地方。因此，对我们来说，要做的工作就是帮助您弄清楚期望的结果是什么，客户正在寻求的更好的生活是什么。你只是把他们送到那里的工具。仅此而已。我的意思是有太多令人厌倦的类比，所以我什至不想使用它们，但是-

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Milkshakes maybe.
turns.zh: 也许是奶昔。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: What's that?
turns.zh: 那是什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The milkshake analogy.
turns.zh: 奶昔的比喻。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: The milkshake one, it's not even the analogy. I think that was one of the original job stories that is the milkshake one.
turns.zh: 奶昔那一类，根本就不是类比。我认为这是最初的工作故事之一，即奶昔故事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Any other things you want to share about the process that you go through with the companies, things you've learned, before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 在我们进行令人兴奋的闪电轮融资之前，您还有什么想分享的关于您与公司合作的过程以及您学到的东西吗？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah. One of the objections that we often get to this type of work is that research takes a long time and that research can often lead to more questions and can slow everything down. You can end up in analysis paralysis, but it doesn't have to be that way. It can be very straightforward, honestly, in a survey scenario. With SparkToro, in just that scenario, I have lots of examples of companies where we ran surveys, it can be a couple of weeks. Two or three weeks, you can actually come out with something solid to move forward with, and you don't get stuck in the bickering or all those stakeholders, the too many cooks in the kitchen. You can come to something decisive. You can get value out of that.
turns.zh: 是的。我们对此类工作经常遇到的反对意见之一是，研究需要很长时间，而且研究往往会导致更多问题，并可能减慢一切。您可能会陷入分析瘫痪，但情况并非一定如此。老实说，在调查场景中，这可能非常简单。对于 SparkToro，在这种情况下，我有很多我们进行调查的公司的例子，这可能需要几周的时间。两到三周的时间，你实际上可以拿出一些可靠的东西来推进，而且你不会陷入争吵或所有利益相关者，厨房里太多厨师的困境。你可以做出决定性的事情。你可以从中获得价值。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: The other thing too, the other objection that we get a lot from founders in particular is because they build products to solve a problem that they had, which is cool and it definitely makes you one of the most knowledgeable people about your solution. But products change, markets change, customers change, teams change in a ball. Not everything can live inside of your head, and there's a ton of value in learning and getting inside the heads of your best customers that you may have been really close to the inception of the product. But if any span of time has changed, you'll always learn something new. I've never been in a scenario like this where a founder has not learned something new from their research and been able to leverage it in a way that makes their product experience better.
turns.zh: 还有一件事，我们从创始人那里得到的很多反对意见是因为他们开发产品来解决他们遇到的问题，这很酷，而且它肯定会让你成为对你的解决方案最了解的人之一。但产品在变化，市场在变化，客户在变化，团队也在发生变化。并不是所有的事情都能存在于你的头脑中，学习和了解你最好的客户的头脑有很大的价值，因为你可能已经非常接近产品的诞生了。但如果时间跨度发生变化，你总会学到新的东西。我从来没有遇到过这样的情况：创始人没有从他们的研究中学到新的东西，并且能够以一种让他们的产品体验更好的方式利用它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. We'll come back to how folks can reach out to you if they want to experience this process, could work with you, learn more. But before we get there, we've gotten into a very exciting lightning round. I've got five quick questions for you. We'll go through them quick, whatever comes to mind. That's what we're doing. Okay, sounds good?
turns.zh: 惊人的。我们将回到人们如何联系您，如果他们想体验这个过程，可以与您合作，了解更多信息。但在我们到达那里之前，我们已经进入了一场非常激动人心的闪电回合。我有五个简单的问题要问你。无论想到什么，我们都会快速浏览它们。这就是我们正在做的事情。好吧，听起来不错吗？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. What are two or three books that you recommend most to people looking to get better at marketing?
turns.zh: 好的。您最向那些希望提高营销水平的人推荐哪两三本书？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: I very, very, very rarely read marketing books, but there's two that I think are pretty foundational and recent. So Obviously Awesome by April Dunford. I'm sure you've heard that one a ton. It's kind of required reading, I would say, especially for founders. I told April when she first wrote, I'm like, "I'm going to require every single founder I work with to read your book before we work with them," because it's foundational, you have to know that.
turns.zh: 我非常非常非常很少读营销书籍，但我认为有两本非常基础且最新的书籍。显然太棒了，作者：April Dunford。我相信你已经听过很多次了。我想说，这是必读的书，尤其是对于创始人而言。当阿普丽尔第一次写信时，我告诉她，“我会要求每一位与我合作的创始人在与他们合作之前阅读你的书，”因为这是基础性的，你必须知道这一点。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: And then the other one that I really enjoyed flip side was Hooked by Nir Eyal. That one was great too. But like I said, I don't read many marketing books. The other one that I would be remiss not to mention is ours that we're writing about the process, which is really about the step by step how to do this thing. So as much as we love going through this process with companies, I sort of took a page from April here too, in that telling the process and having people be able to rule this out and do this internally themselves has been wildly gratifying. We do it with a training program and this is our next step in getting out into the world even more. So you absolutely can do this stuff yourself. So that process is later in that book. And then another book that I read recently, which has nothing to do with marketing at all, but was really nice was 4000 Weeks. I don't think-
turns.zh: 另外一个我真正喜欢的另一面是 Nir ​​Eyal 的《Hooked》。那个也很棒。但就像我说的，我读的营销书籍不多。另一件我不提的疏忽是我们正在写的过程，这实际上是关于如何一步一步地做这件事。因此，尽管我们非常喜欢与公司一起经历这个过程，但我也借鉴了四月份的经验，因为讲述这个过程并让人们能够排除这种情况并自己在内部执行此操作一直是非常令人满意的。我们通过培训计划来做到这一点，这是我们进一步走向世界的下一步。所以你绝对可以自己做这些事情。所以这个过程在那本书的后面。我最近读的另一本书是《4000 Weeks》，与营销完全无关，但非常好。我不认为——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm reading that right now.
turns.zh: 我现在正在读。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Oh yeah, I enjoyed it. It was a nice sort of coming back to base a bit. I don't know when I read it. I just finished it a couple of weeks ago. It was just the timing was perfect. I feel like what's going on in the world right now and how everybody's probably feeling right now, it's a good solid read for now.
turns.zh: 哦，是的，我很享受。回到基地真是太好了。我不知道我什么时候读到的。我几周前刚刚完成。只是时机非常完美。我觉得现在世界上正在发生什么，以及每个人现在可能的感受，这是一本很好的、可靠的读物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm enjoying it. I just started. I'm glad to-
turns.zh: 我很享受。我刚刚开始。我很高兴——

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, you encouraged me to keep reading it.
turns.zh: 好吧，你鼓励我继续读下去。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Okay. Favorite recent movie or TV show?
turns.zh: 好的。最近最喜欢的电影或电视节目？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: I have young kids. I just bought a second property. We're renovating three houses right now. I do not watch movies almost ever. The only thing that I'm currently binging is YouTubers that do DIY interior design and renos. Reason being my partner and I bought a property with four very, very old cottages lakefront, almost like tiny houses, little cottages. We are slowly renovating each of them. So my sort of fill is learning about interior design and DIY home rentals. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我有年幼的孩子。我刚刚购买了第二处房产。我们现在正在装修三栋房子。我几乎从不看电影。我目前唯一喜欢的是 DIY 室内设计和装修的 YouTuber。原因是我和我的伴侣在湖边买了一套有四栋非常非常古老的小屋的房产，几乎就像小房子、小小屋。我们正在慢慢地翻新它们中的每一个。所以我的兴趣就是学习室内设计和 DIY 房屋租赁。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Who's had the most impact on you in your career?
turns.zh: 在您的职业生涯中，谁对您影响最大？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: This is the worst question. I hate saying this, but it's probably my dad. I have to say my dad because he's an entrepreneur through and through. And I remember very vividly, I worked for him for I think eight years early in my career. One of the things that he always said was like, "It was the joy of the business." He didn't care what, he's like, "It doesn't matter what you're selling." He could be selling anything, but it was the joy of entrepreneurship. And that really stuck with me. So even when I was in house, I always knew that I needed to do something on my own and be in charge of that journey. His joy in it has impacted me a lot. He was the reason why I knew I was always going to do this.
turns.zh: 这是最糟糕的问题。我讨厌这么说，但这可能是我爸爸。我不得不说我的父亲，因为他是一位彻头彻尾的企业家。我记得非常清楚，在我职业生涯的早期，我为他工作了八年。他总是说的一件事是，“这是生意的乐趣。”他不在乎什么，他就像，“你卖什么并不重要。”他可以卖任何东西，但这是创业的乐趣。这真的让我难以忘怀。因此，即使当我在家时，我也始终知道我需要自己做一些事情并负责这段旅程。他的快乐对我影响很大。他是我知道我总是会这样做的原因。

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Other than that, I would say I have an incredible network of women that I have been very lucky. We're part of a group that we call Shine Crew. I think I'm supposed to copyright that or something to somebody because I think the term Shine Theory is what it's based on basically. But I'm very, very lucky to be heavily influenced by April Dunford, Tara Robertson, Joanna Wiebe, Talia Wolf. And then obviously my business partner, Claire, obviously changed everything for me. Having that partnership in business, I don't think I would've lasted this long. So yeah, definitely a huge influence for sure.
turns.zh: 除此之外，我想说我拥有一个令人难以置信的女性网络，我非常幸运。我们是 Shine Crew 团队的成员。我认为我应该将其或其他东西的版权授予某人，因为我认为“闪耀理论”一词基本上就是它的基础。但我非常非常幸运地受到阿普丽尔·邓福德、塔拉·罗伯逊、乔安娜·维贝、塔利亚·沃尔夫的影响。显然，我的商业伙伴克莱尔显然改变了我的一切。有了这种商业伙伴关系，我想我不会坚持这么久。所以，是的，肯定会产生巨大的影响。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's one thing that helps you stay focused and productive during the day?
turns.zh: 有什么事情可以帮助您在一天中保持专注和高效？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: Definitely carving up time, like time blocking. I do a lot of time blocking in advance with a little brain emoji of safeguarding my time. Because we're a small team and we use Slack obviously, something else that we do to protect each other's time is not time stamp, but we put a little code in all of our messages that's either like, "You don't have to listen to this before the end of the day," or, "It's timely," or, "It's no rush," so that we know when we need to mentally process messages in Slack, so we can drop in there just periodically. And then the only other thing that I would say that I do maybe once a month or once a quarter is, we're pretty buttoned up about our time tracking, so we go back and it sort of keeps us honest about how our time is actually spent. And then we can sort of adjust and time block accordingly to make up for the shortcomings of our previous quarter.
turns.zh: 绝对是分割时间，就像时间阻塞一样。我会提前用一些大脑表情符号来阻止很多时间，以保护我的时间。因为我们是一个小团队，而且我们显然使用 Slack，所以我们为保护彼此的时间所做的其他事情不是时间戳，而是我们在所有消息中添加了一些代码，例如“您不必在一天结束之前听这个”，或者“很及时”，或者“不着急”，这样我们就知道何时需要在 Slack 中在心里处理消息，这样我们就可以定期去那里。然后我想说的唯一一件事是，我可能每月一次或每季度一次，我们对时间跟踪非常保守，所以我们回去，这让我们诚实地了解我们的时间实际上是如何度过的。然后我们可以相应地进行调整和时间限制，以弥补上一季度的缺陷。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That was really clever. I haven't heard of that trick. What's the emoji for "You can do this later"?
turns.zh: 这真是太聪明了。我没听说过这个伎俩。 “你可以稍后再做”的表情符号是什么？

turns.speaker: Georgiana Laudi
turns.en: We actually just use no rush or EOD for end of day, or timely. We do have the alarm emoji, is the "Now. This is going to be dealt with ASAP."
turns.zh: 实际上，我们只是在一天结束时或及时使用“不加急”或“EOD”。我们确实有警报表情符号，即“现在。我们将尽快处理此问题。”

turns.en: Amazing. Gia, thank you for making time. For this final question, where can folks find you online? How do they pre-order your book? How can they learn more? And then also, just how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 惊人的。 Gia，谢谢您抽出时间。对于最后一个问题，人们可以在哪里在线找到您？他们如何预订您的书？他们如何才能了解更多？还有，听众如何对你有用？

If you want any templates or whatever that don't get included in the show notes, just ping me. I've no problem with that. And then forgetthefunnel.com, we've got a book page where there is a wait list for the... Well, we're going to do presale, and then the published physical book will be early in 2023. But we are going to do presale because... Get it in those hands. Why not?
turns.zh: 谢谢你的询问。 Twitter 可能是最好的方式。我的 Twitter 账号太糟糕了，@ggiiaa 是我的 Twitter。显然，我偶尔会使用 LinkedIn。我的电子邮件地址是 gia@forgetthefunnel.com。因此，如果有人有任何疑问，请随时给我发电子邮件。如果您想要任何模板或任何未包含在演出说明中的内容，请联系我。我对此没有问题。然后忘记thefunnel.com，我们有一个图书页面，其中有一个等待名单......好吧，我们将进行预售，然后出版的实体书将在 2023 年初上市。但我们将进行预售，因为......把它送到那些人手中。为什么不呢？
